introduction: A replacement Pod can recover a process while losing its data. A persistent volume changes that lifecycle, but does not itself supply an independent backup. You will test process replacement and logical restoration as separate experiments.

This lab runs one PostgreSQL instance on kind local storage, then connects the existing authenticated Taskboard adapter. It is deliberately not highly available: the laptop and its Docker storage remain shared failure points. CloudNativePG can automate database-specific behavior, but its operator does not eliminate storage durability, backup, upgrade or recovery responsibilities.
prerequisites: Ubuntu 24.04 Bash in WSL2 or a disposable Linux VM; Docker is running. Use the same terminal unless a step names a second terminal.

Week28 recovered policy cluster and app-secure.yaml/service.yaml. Supplied Taskboard image contains reference.stage07 and reference.migrate. ~/dev-opps-lab/evidence must have space for the small dump.

concepts.title: Claim, volume and storage class
paragraphs: A PersistentVolumeClaim asks for storage capacity/access mode. A StorageClass defines how a provisioner creates a volume. The resulting volume has its own lifecycle and reclaim policy. A StatefulSet preserves each replica identity and claim association across Pod replacement.
concepts.example: postgres-0 reconnects to data-postgres-0 after replacement.
concepts.judgment: A kind local-path volume is still on one computer. Retaining a claim protects from a Pod restart, not disk corruption or laptop loss.

concepts.title: Operator, replication and recoverability
paragraphs: An operator adds a database-specific API and reconciliation logic for actions such as bootstrap, replication and failover. CloudNativePG uses a Cluster resource; current backup guidance supports CNPG-I plugins, including the Barman Cloud Plugin. The plugin and object-store credentials are additional dependencies to operate.

A standby may promptly replicate an accidental deletion. A historical backup plus retained transaction history addresses a different problem. A logical dump can restore selected data independently, but is not the same as continuous point-in-time recovery.
concepts.example: A successful restore into a separate database proves more than a successful backup job.
concepts.judgment: For a small team, managed PostgreSQL can reduce operational burden. Compare restore procedure, RPO/RTO, upgrades and ownership rather than merely installation effort.

steps.title: Create persistent PostgreSQL
steps.purpose: Keep credentials out of the manifest and observe the storage objects.

commands.code:
export KUBECONFIG="$HOME/dev-opps-lab/k8s/kubeconfig"
kubectl config current-context
cd "$HOME/dev-opps-lab/k8s"
kubectl get storageclass
kubectl -n devopps get deployment postgres
kubectl -n devopps delete deployment postgres --ignore-not-found --cascade=foreground --wait=true
PG_PASSWORD=$(python3 -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(24))')
kubectl -n devopps create secret generic pg-auth --from-literal=password="$PG_PASSWORD"
cat > postgres.yaml <<'YAML'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: postgres, namespace: devopps}
spec:
  selector: {app: postgres}
  ports: [{port: 5432, targetPort: 5432}]
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata: {name: postgres, namespace: devopps}
spec:
  serviceName: postgres
  replicas: 1
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: postgres}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: postgres}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: postgres
        image: postgres:17
        env:
        - name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
          valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: pg-auth, key: password}}
        - {name: PGDATA, value: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata}
        ports: [{containerPort: 5432}]
        readinessProbe:
          exec: {command: [pg_isready, -U, postgres]}
          periodSeconds: 3
        resources:
          requests: {cpu: 100m, memory: 128Mi}
          limits: {memory: 256Mi}
        volumeMounts: [{name: data, mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql/data}]
  volumeClaimTemplates:
  - metadata: {name: data}
    spec:
      accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
      storageClassName: standard
      resources: {requests: {storage: 1Gi}}
YAML
kubectl apply -f postgres.yaml
kubectl -n devopps rollout status statefulset/postgres --timeout=180s
kubectl -n devopps get pvc
kubectl get pv
explain: Remove only week 27's disposable postgres Deployment before introducing the StatefulSet. Both otherwise carry app=postgres, so the same Service would randomly route to two different databases. That old network-probe database contains no Taskboard data; preserve it first if you added any.
Confirm the kind standard StorageClass exists before applying. Generate one random password and store it in a lab Secret; do not commit credentials or a Secret export.

The full manifest creates a Service and single-replica StatefulSet. volumeClaimTemplates creates data-postgres-0; ReadWriteOnce permits attachment for writing by one node. PGDATA selects a data subdirectory, and pg_isready probes whether PostgreSQL accepts connections.
rollout waits for the instance; get pvc/pv shows binding and reclaim policy. Storage capacity here is requested capacity, not a promise of independent disk durability.
commands.expected: postgres-0 Ready; data-postgres-0 Bound to a volume.
commands.troubleshoot: A Pending claim requires inspecting StorageClass and provisioner events; deleting the database Pod cannot create a missing storage class.

steps.checkpoint: Record the volume reclaim policy and where the bytes physically live.

steps.title: Connect Taskboard and run its explicit migration
steps.purpose: Persist application data and retain separate liveness/readiness contracts.

commands.code:
ALICE_TOKEN=$(python3 -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))')
BOB_TOKEN=$(python3 -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))')
kubectl -n devopps create secret generic taskboard-env --from-literal=DATABASE_URL="postgresql://postgres:$PG_PASSWORD@postgres:5432/postgres" --from-literal=LAB_ALICE_TOKEN="$ALICE_TOKEN" --from-literal=LAB_BOB_TOKEN="$BOB_TOKEN"
cat > migration-network.yaml <<'YAML'
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: {name: database-migration, namespace: devopps}
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels: {app: postgres}
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
  ingress:
  - from:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels: {app: taskboard-migrate}
    ports:
    - {protocol: TCP, port: 5432}
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: {name: migration-egress, namespace: devopps}
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels: {app: taskboard-migrate}
  policyTypes: [Egress]
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels: {app: postgres}
    ports:
    - {protocol: TCP, port: 5432}
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels: {kubernetes.io/metadata.name: kube-system}
      podSelector:
        matchLabels: {k8s-app: kube-dns}
    ports:
    - {protocol: UDP, port: 53}
    - {protocol: TCP, port: 53}
YAML
kubectl apply -f migration-network.yaml
cat > migration.yaml <<'YAML'
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata: {name: taskboard-migrate, namespace: devopps}
spec:
  backoffLimit: 0
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: taskboard-migrate}}
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
      - name: migrate
        image: devopps-taskboard:w25
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        command: [python, -m, reference.migrate]
        envFrom: [{secretRef: {name: taskboard-env}}]
YAML
kubectl apply -f migration.yaml
kubectl -n devopps wait --for=condition=complete job/taskboard-migrate --timeout=120s
cat > database-app.json <<'JSON'
{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"app","command":["python","-m","uvicorn","reference.stage07:app","--host","0.0.0.0","--port","8000","--no-access-log"],"envFrom":[{"secretRef":{"name":"taskboard-env"}}],"readinessProbe":{"httpGet":{"path":"/readyz","port":"http"}}}]}}}}
JSON
kubectl patch --local -f app-secure.yaml --type=strategic --patch-file database-app.json -o yaml > app-database.yaml
kubectl apply -f app-database.yaml
kubectl -n devopps rollout status deployment/taskboard --timeout=180s
explain: Two distinct random tokens identify local teaching users. DATABASE_URL includes the database credential; the Secret is passed by reference into the Job and app. These opaque tokens are for a private lab, not a public identity system.

Week 27's database policy permits only app=taskboard. Give the migration Job its own app=taskboard-migrate label and a narrowly scoped database ingress/DNS-and-database egress policy. Do not reuse the application label: the HTTP Service would otherwise select a migration Pod. NetworkPolicy grants are additive; the original application rule remains in force.
The Job runs the supplied idempotent migrations exactly once; backoffLimit0 avoids blindly repeating a failed migration. wait checks completion. Read its logs if it fails.

The local strategic patch switches to stage07, injects the Secret and checks /readyz for database schema availability. /livez stays independent. This lab deliberately shares the database owner role; production needs a restricted runtime SQL role distinct from migration authority.
commands.expected: Migration completes; stage07 has /readyz200 and /tasks requires a lab token.
commands.troubleshoot: If readiness503 inspect Job logs and database connectivity/schema. Never change liveness to depend on the database.

steps.checkpoint: In terminal2 run kubectl -n devopps port-forward service/taskboard 18000:80 --address 127.0.0.1; keep it running for the next step.

steps.title: Test restart and restore independently
steps.purpose: Write a task, replace the database process, then restore a dump into another database.

commands.code:
curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $ALICE_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title":"storage-survives-restart"}' http://127.0.0.1:18000/tasks
kubectl -n devopps delete pod postgres-0
kubectl -n devopps rollout status statefulset/postgres --timeout=180s
curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $ALICE_TOKEN" http://127.0.0.1:18000/tasks
mkdir -p "$HOME/dev-opps-lab/evidence/w29"
kubectl -n devopps exec postgres-0 -- pg_dump -U postgres -d postgres -Fc > "$HOME/dev-opps-lab/evidence/w29/taskboard.dump"
kubectl -n devopps exec postgres-0 -- createdb -U postgres restore_lab
kubectl -n devopps exec -i postgres-0 -- pg_restore -U postgres -d restore_lab --no-owner --no-privileges < "$HOME/dev-opps-lab/evidence/w29/taskboard.dump"
kubectl -n devopps exec postgres-0 -- psql -U postgres -d restore_lab -c 'SELECT title FROM tasks;'
explain: curl -f fails on HTTP errors; headers provide the teaching identity and JSON body type. Task creation must survive replacement because the same claim is reattached.

pg_dump -Fc writes a custom-format logical backup to local evidence via stdout redirection. createdb creates a separate restore target; it does not overwrite the source. exec -i passes stdin from the local dump into pg_restore; --no-owner/--no-privileges avoids replaying ownership/grants from another environment.
The final SQL query checks actual restored content. Protect the dump as data; it is not a credential-free artifact just because it is binary.
commands.expected: The named task remains after Pod replacement and appears in restore_lab.
commands.troubleshoot: If tables are missing inspect migration schema and dump listing (pg_restore -l). A restored database existing is not evidence its task data is correct.

steps.checkpoint: Write separate claims: restart survival, logical restore, and unproven machine-loss recovery.

failure.title: A claim asks for a nonexistent storage class
failure.boundary: Create a new empty claim; do not alter the working database claim.

inject.code:
cat > missing-storage.yaml <<'YAML'
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: missing-storage, namespace: devopps}
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: intentionally-absent
  resources: {requests: {storage: 1Gi}}
YAML
kubectl apply -f missing-storage.yaml
explain: The new claim asks for an unavailable provisioner class.
inject.troubleshoot: Wait briefly then inspect events, not application logs.

investigate.code:
kubectl -n devopps describe pvc missing-storage
kubectl get storageclass
explain: Compare requested class with actual classes.
investigate.troubleshoot: Some provisioners delay binding until a consumer exists; distinguish that event from class-not-found.

hints: Which component could provision the claim?

explanation: The storage request cannot be fulfilled by the named class. A Pod using it would remain unschedulable for storage reasons; restarting that Pod would preserve the bad claim request.

explain: Remove only the empty fault claim.
recover.expected: Fault claim deleted; healthy database claim unchanged.

verification.code:
kubectl -n devopps get pvc data-postgres-0
kubectl -n devopps exec postgres-0 -- psql -U postgres -d restore_lab -c 'SELECT count(*) FROM tasks;'
explain: Check surviving bound claim and independently restored data.
verification.expected: Bound claim; task count at least1.
verification.troubleshoot: Inspect whether you queried source or target database.

questions.answer: No. It proves reattachment after process replacement. Corrupt or lost underlying storage requires a separate recoverable copy.

questions.prompt: Would a standby undo accidental DELETE?
questions.answer: Usually the bad transaction too. Point-in-time recovery uses historical state plus transaction history, with tested restoration.
It reconciles database resources and procedures such as replicas/failover. You still own access, retention, capacity, restore validation and decisions about acceptable loss.

exercise.brief: Compare this StatefulSet, CloudNativePG and managed PostgreSQL.
deliverables: Decision with backup, upgrade and failure owners
acceptance: No claim of HA from the local instance
Recovery route works without the original application Pod
hints: Include storage failure as well as process failure.
solution: Prefer a managed database when its recovery and cost model meet the small-team requirement. An operator is justified only with capacity to maintain its controller, storage, plugins and upgrades.

cleanup.code:
kubectl -n devopps exec postgres-0 -- dropdb -U postgres restore_lab
kubectl -n devopps delete job taskboard-migrate
kubectl -n devopps delete networkpolicy database-migration migration-egress
explain: Remove the independent restore target and completed migration Job. Retain source DB, PVC and Taskboard for week30; stop port-forward with Ctrl+C.
Remove only the temporary migration policies after the completed Job is deleted; retain the application/database boundary policies.
cleanup.troubleshoot: Do not delete data-postgres-0 until evidence is exported and the local source is deliberately disposable.

references.title: Kubernetes NetworkPolicy selection and additive rules
references.usedFor: Separate application and migration identities while preserving the database ingress boundary.

repoConnections.principle: Failover and backup solve different failures.
repoConnections.application: Compare the successful Pod replacement and independent logical restore; require both classes of evidence in the placement decision.

notes: No PostgreSQL/Kubernetes container execution occurred on the authoring host; run the checks in the defined learner environment.
title: Understand state and operators
outcome: Explain Kubernetes storage and the operational cost of running a database in a cluster.
